A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bottlenecked Transformer research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark accuracies and training-budget, reconsolidation-budget and processor-size experiments in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds latent-rollout comparisons, a recent-window ablation and measurements of cache rewrites.

M1.justification: Section 6.4 adds a fixed-token invocation variant for the window ablation: processing occurs after the prompt and every R tokens instead of at newline boundaries. This limited inference adaptation leaves the main architecture, KV selection, gated rewrites and training objectives unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on 128k OpenMathInstruct-2 examples and evaluate GSM8K, MATH, SVAMP, TheoremQA, LogiQA, Gaokao-MathQA and GSM-Hard. The added analyses reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds one comparator, SFT with Coconut-inspired latent rollout, for all four backbones. The existing SFT and pause-token comparators remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include fixed invocation intervals R={16,32,48,64,96} and pre/post-rewrite cosine-distance measurements on GSM8K. The added baseline uses 16 latent steps after the prefix. Existing experiments retain their training budgets, backbones and greedy pass@1 evaluation.

E4.justification: Sections 6.4–6.5 substantially extend the analyses by testing sensitivity to consolidation timing and directly examining rewrite behavior across processing steps, layers and heads. The earlier epoch, top-k and processor-size ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed results, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. Figure 4's mean cosine distances summarize rewrite behavior rather than introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds findings on latent-rollout failure, window sensitivity and internal rewrite behavior. For example, the new Llama 3.1 8B latent-rollout GSM8K score is 4.02%, alongside unchanged SFT and Bottleneck scores of 70.28% and 71.87%. Table 3 adds window-dependent accuracies, and Figure 4 shows predominantly value-vector changes. Existing scores and ablation curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: The separate bounds displayed in v4's Theorem 4.2 already appear in v3 Appendix A.3, Eqs. 19 and 26. The definitions and mathematical derivations are retained; the softened maximization language changes interpretation rather than introducing a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same contributions: an information-bottleneck rationale, selective KV consolidation/reconsolidation and reasoning improvements reaching +6.6 percentage points on selected tasks/backbones.

C2.justification: Theorem 4.2's title and accompanying explanation soften maximization to encouragement of high mutual information. New interpretations address schedule robustness and editing memory content rather than addressing, with early-layer concentration. Section 6.5 explicitly qualifies rewrite magnitude as an indirect signal, not a measurement of information compression.

D1.justification: v4 documents the new baseline's hidden-state feedback and 16-step prefix rollout, together with invocation details for the window ablation. Appendix D's existing hyperparameters, parameter counts and computational-overhead disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6.1 explicitly connects the new baseline to Coconut and discusses its underperformance relative to that work's reported accuracy–efficiency tradeoff. Hao et al. was already cited; the bibliography and broader ALSC taxonomy remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized language corrections, rewrites the theoretical explanation, expands the experimental narrative and adds Sections 6.4–6.5. It removes redundant introductory text and the duplicate subsection heading in Appendix C, and updates the conference header.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains baseline rows, while Table 3 and the six-panel rewrite Figure 4 are added. Figure 2 is repositioned; the unchanged processor-size plot becomes Figure 5, and the parameter-count table becomes Table 4. The overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: The additional comparator, window ablation and rewrite diagnostics improve scrutiny of robustness and processor behavior while retaining the original evidence. More cautious interpretation also helps. The gain remains limited because latent-rollout training is sparsely documented and rewrite distances do not directly establish information compression.
